Carta is built on researched data and clear rules. AI is used in four places, and each place is deliberately limited: it chooses from or rephrases what Carta already knows, and code checks it before you see it. This page says where, with which model, what it cannot do and how you let us know if it is wrong. Where we measured something, the number is here. Where not, that is stated too.

Ratings, prices, month suitability, crowds, the map, the filters and the ranking in Discover are calculated by code from data. No model decides about that. The first answer in Ask Carta is also built by code.

What it does: answer a question in plain words, in each of the six app languages. Code writes the first answer: a short list of places with prices and months. A model can then add a few sentences that quote numbered notes.

Model and provider: Qwen3 30B (Qwen team) on Cloudflare Workers AI, with Llama 3.2 3B (Meta) as fallback. If you turn it on, a small model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B) runs on your own device and your question never leaves it.

What it cannot do: it knows nothing outside the Carta catalogue, it cannot book or check live availability, and it can still miss a place that suits you. Prices are estimates and keep their "~". It never invents a number: every number in a sentence must be in a note, otherwise the sentence is dropped.

How it is checked: every sentence must quote a note, and every place and every number in it is compared with the notes and the maps on the screen. If more than 30 percent of the sentences fail, the written answer is withdrawn and only the answer built by code remains. With every change to Ask a fixed set of 200 questions in six languages is run, and a change that lowers the score cannot be merged.

Measured on that set (retrieval on rules only, the weakest setting): for 93 percent of the questions at least one of the places a traveller would expect is in the first ten, and on average 57 percent of the expected places. The facts on which a sentence rests reach the model correctly in 99,6 percent of 689 checks. Of 30 questions that Carta must refuse (outside Europe, no travel answer) 25 are refused, and 2 questions within scope were refused by accident. The hybrid search with the full index has not been measured yet.
What it does: turns your city and your answers into a walking day, chosen from a set of at most 24 own places of Carta, with a line about why each stop fits.
Model and provider: Gemini Flash-Lite models from Google, tried in order if one is busy. For paying travellers who tick events, Google Search is used to find at most two festivals or markets.

What it cannot do: it cannot add a place to your route that Carta does not have. A stop must be a real place from the set, with Carta's name and position, not the model's. Found events are shown as "check this year's dates" and are never included in the route. Opening hours are not guaranteed.

How it is checked: the server drops every stop that is not in the set, and double stops, and code recalculates the times of day and drops legs that are too long to walk. If the model fails or returns too little, you get Carta's built-in planner instead and you get your plan credit back.

Measured: a set of 20 test cities where Carta's reference plans meet every rule (20 of 20). We have an automatic assessor that agrees with our rules with kappa 0,90 on 40 example plans. We have not yet measured this against human assessments, so we claim no quality score for the model's plans.
What it does: suggests three to five cities for a day trip based on the description you type. Paying travellers can also get real places outside the Carta catalogue, found with Google Search.
Model and provider: the same Gemini models from Google as with day plans.

What it cannot do: a suggestion from the catalogue must be a real city from the catalogue; a web discovery needs coordinates within 400 km of your stay. It does not check whether a discovered place is open or good. See web discoveries as pointers.
What it does: reads the confirmations you put in (pdf, photo, text or link) and fills in empty booking fields of your trip. It never overwrites what you typed yourself.
Model and provider: Gemini models from Google. The documents you add are sent to Google for this one request, and Carta keeps the result for 24 hours so that you do not pay twice.
What it cannot do: it only reports what is in the document and drops links that were not in it. A wrongly read code or amount is possible, so check every row that it fills in.

Write to us with the question you asked, what you saw and what you expected. The more exact, the faster we can reproduce it. Wrong answers are how the checks above get better: a reproducible case is added to the test sets. A report button in the app is planned.

No decision about you is made by AI. Nothing here influences your account, your price or your access. You can always ignore a suggestion, and every AI function has a route without AI: the facts answer, the built-in day planner and the ordinary city list.

Our reading is that these functions are not high-risk systems, and that the transparency obligation applies to Carta: you must know that you are dealing with AI and that text was written by a model. This page and the model cards are how we comply with that now; a visible label with every AI answer is still to come. Carta uses general models from others (Google, Alibaba Cloud, Meta); their makers bear the obligations for the models themselves. This is a plain-language summary by the team, not legal advice, and a lawyer will review it.

A trip planner can unnoticed favour famous places. We compare how many places Carta has in each of the 43 countries and 310 regions with what the size, population and tourist overnight stays would lead one to expect, and publish the table. The last run found 10 countries with too few places (including Germany, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Moldova at every weighting we tried), 26 regions, 24 gaps in missing fields and 5 languages where the intro is still only in English. Every gap has a line in the backlog. The table is not a remedy: it shows where the AI answers are probably thinner. It is in the project documentation as docs/data/coverage-parity.md.

A model card for Ask Carta and one for day plans tell in more detail what each is built for, what it was tested on and what the known weak points are. A third card for the place tagger is a stub: that model does not exist yet. They are in the project documentation under docs/ai/.

Carta builds on researched data and clear rules. AI is used in four places, and each is deliberately limited: It selects or rephrases what Carta already knows, and code checks it before you see it. This page says where, with which model, what it cannot do and how you report to us when it is wrong. Where we have measured something, the number is here. Where not, that is stated there too.

Ratings, prices, month suitability, crowds, the map, the filters and the ranking in Explore are calculated by code from data. No model decides about that. The first answer in Ask Carta is also built by code.

What it does: answers a question in simple words, in each of the six app languages. Code writes the first answer: a short list of places with prices and months. A model can then add a few sentences that cite numbered notes.

Model and provider: Qwen3 30B (Qwen team) on Cloudflare Workers AI, with Llama 3.2 3B (Meta) as fallback. If you switch it on, a small model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B) runs on your own device instead, and your question never leaves it.

What it cannot do: It knows nothing outside Carta's catalogue, cannot book or check live availability and can still overlook a fitting place. Prices are estimates and keep their '~'. It never invents a number: Every number in a sentence must be in a note, otherwise the sentence is dropped.

How it is checked: Every sentence must cite a note, and every place and every number in it is compared with the notes and the maps on the screen. If more than 30 percent of the sentences fail, the written answer is withdrawn and only the one built by code remains. A fixed set of 200 questions in six languages runs with every change to Ask, and a change that lowers the value cannot be adopted.

Measured on this set (search with rules only, the weakest setting): For 93 percent of the questions, at least one of the places a traveller would expect is among the first ten, and on average it is 57 percent of the expected places. The facts a sentence is based on reach the model correctly in 99,6 percent of 689 checks. Of 30 questions that Carta should decline (outside Europe, no travel answer), 25 are declined, and 2 questions within scope were declined by mistake. The hybrid search with the full index is not yet measured.
What it does: makes a day on foot out of your place and your answers, chosen from a stack of up to 24 own places of Carta, with a line on why each stop fits.
Model and provider: Gemini Flash Lite models from Google, tried in turn when one is busy. For paying travellers who tick events, the Google search is used to find up to two festivals or markets.

What it cannot do: It cannot add a place to your route that Carta does not have. A stop must be a real place from the stack, with name and position from Carta, not from the model. Found events are shown as 'confirm dates this year' and never taken into the route. Opening hours are not guaranteed.

How it is checked: The server throws out every stop that is not in the stack, and duplicate stops, and code re-times the day and strikes legs that are too far to walk. If the model fails or delivers too little, you get Carta's built-in planner, and your plan quota is returned.

Measured: a set of 20 test places where Carta's reference plans satisfy every rule (20 of 20). We have an automatic rater that agrees with our rules at kappa 0,90 on 40 sample plans. We have not yet measured it against human ratings, so we claim no quality value for the model's plans.

What it does: suggests three to five places for a day trip, according to the description that you enter. Paying travellers can also get real places beyond Carta's catalogue, found with the Google search.
Model and provider: the same Gemini models from Google as for the day plans.

What it cannot do: A suggestion from the catalogue must be a real catalogue place; a discovery from the web needs coordinates within 400 km around your accommodation. It does not check whether a discovered place is open or good. Treat web discoveries as clues.
What it does: reads the confirmations that you put in (PDF, photo, text or link) and fills empty booking fields of your trip. It never overwrites what you typed.
Model and provider: Gemini models from Google. The documents that you add go to Google for this one request, and Carta keeps the result for 24 hours so that you do not pay twice.
What it cannot do: It reports only what is in the document and leaves out links that were not in it. A wrongly read code or amount is possible, so check every line that it fills.

Carta is based on verified data and simple rules. The AI is used in four points, and each is limited on purpose: it chooses among what Carta already knows or rephrases it, and the code checks it before you see it. This page says where, with which model, what it cannot do and how to report to us when it gets it wrong. Where we have measured something, the number is here. Where we haven't, we say so.

Ratings, prices, suitability by month, crowding, map, filters and ranking in Explore are calculated by the code from the data. No model decides them. Even the first answer of Ask Carta is built by the code.

What it does: answers a question in simple words, in any of the app's six languages. The code writes the first answer: a short list of places with prices and months. A model can then add some sentences that cite numbered notes.

Model and provider: Qwen3 30B (Qwen team) on Cloudflare Workers AI, with Llama 3.2 3B (Meta) as reserve. If you turn it on, a small model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B) runs on your device and your question never leaves it.

What it cannot do: it knows nothing outside Carta's catalogue, it cannot book or check availability in real time, and it can still miss a place suited to you. Prices are estimates and keep the "~". It never invents a figure: every number in a sentence must appear in a note, otherwise the sentence is discarded.

How it is checked: every sentence must cite a note, and every place and figure within it is compared with the notes and with the cards on screen. If more than 30 percent of the sentences do not pass, the written answer is withdrawn and only the one built by the code remains. A fixed set of 200 questions in six languages is run at every change to Ask, and a change that lowers the score cannot be merged.

Measured on that set (retrieval with rules only, the weakest setting): at least one of the places that a traveller would expect is among the top ten for 93 percent of the questions, and on average 57 percent of the expected places are present. The facts on which a sentence is based reach the model correctly in 99.6 percent of 689 checks. Of the 30 questions that Carta should refuse (outside Europe, without a travel answer), 25 are refused, and 2 pertinent questions were refused by mistake. The hybrid search with the full index is not yet measured.
What it does: turns your city and your answers into a day on foot, chosen from a deck of up to 24 places of Carta's own, with a line on why each stop is suitable.
Model and provider: Gemini Flash-Lite models of Google, tried in order if one is busy. For paying travellers who tick the events, Google Search is used to find up to two festivals or markets.

What it cannot do: it cannot add to your route a place that Carta does not have. A stop must be a real place of the deck, with name and position taken from Carta, not from the model. The events it finds are shown as "confirm this year's dates" and never enter the route. Opening hours are not guaranteed.

How it is checked: the server discards every stop that is not in the deck and the duplicate ones, and the code recalculates the times of the day and eliminates the journeys too long to do on foot. If the model fails or returns too little, you receive Carta's built-in planner and your plan credit is returned to you.

Measured: a set of 20 test cities in which Carta's reference plans respect every rule (20 out of 20). We have an automatic judge that agrees with our rules with kappa 0.90 on 40 example plans. We have not yet compared it with human ratings, so we do not claim a quality score for the model's plans.
What it does: suggests three to five cities for a day trip from the description you write. Paying travellers can also get real places beyond Carta's catalogue, found with Google Search.
Model and provider: the same Gemini models of Google as the daily plans.

What it cannot do: a suggestion from the catalogue must be a real city of the catalogue; a discovery from the web requires coordinates within 400 km of your stay. It does not verify that a discovered place is open or worth it. Treat it as a hint.
What it does: reads the confirmations you upload (PDF, photos, text or links) and fills in the empty fields of the bookings in your trip. It never overwrites what you have written.
Model and provider: Gemini models of Google. The documents you add are sent to Google for this request only, and Carta keeps the result for 24 hours so you don't pay twice.
What it cannot do: it reports only what is printed in the document and discards links that were not there. A misread code or amount is possible, so check every line it fills in.

Write us the question you asked, what you saw and what you expected. The more precise it is, the faster we can reproduce it. Wrong answers are what improves the checks above: a reproducible case is added to the test sets. A report button in the app is planned.

No decision about you is made by the AI. None of this affects your account, your price or your access. You can always ignore a suggestion, and every AI feature has an alternative without AI: the answer with the facts, the built-in daily planner and the normal list of cities.

In our view these features are not high-risk systems, and what applies to Carta is the transparency obligation: you must know that you are dealing with AI and that a text was written by a model. This page and the model cards are the way we comply with it today; a visible label on every AI answer is still to come. Carta uses generic models built by others (Google, Alibaba Cloud, Meta); their authors have the obligations relating to the models themselves. This is a summary in plain words made by the team, not legal advice, and it will be checked by a lawyer.

A trip planner can favour famous places without saying so. We compare how many places Carta has in each of the 43 countries and 310 regions with how many size, population and tourist nights would suggest, and we publish the table. The latest analysis found 10 countries with too few places (including Germany, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Moldova with every weighting method tried), 26 regions, 24 gaps for missing fields and 5 languages in which the introduction is still only in English. Every gap has a row in the backlog. The table is not a cure: it shows where the AI's answers will probably be poorer. It is found in the project documentation as docs/data/coverage-parity.md.
